new_rows.claim: The 4×4 fixpoint solver in exp6_solve.zig supports parallel Jacobi iteration with a --threads N flag. When N=1, the exact serial Gauss-Seidel path is used (byte-identical to the pre-T312 code). When N>1, parallel Jacobi sweeps are used — provably convergent to the same fixpoint (monotone operator on complete lattice), deterministically identical result regardless of thread count or scheduling. Per-thread memory overhead is 2 × 99,133,036 bytes ≈ 189 MB for L_next + H_next. Race controls: 4 tests wired into zig build test — serial-vs-parallel agreement on a synthetic DAG (3 tests, 100+50+10 reps each, 2/4/7 threads), plus a seeded-defect positive control (missing join barrier detected).
new_rows.wrong_answer_pass_rate: 0% (3 agreement tests pass 100% of reps; seeded defect catches 1/1 missing-barrier)

notes:
T312 — PARALLEL 4×4 FIXPOINT IMPLEMENTATION.

=== WHAT I DID ===
1. Added num_threads parameter to run_fixpoint_4x4() in exp6_solve.zig. When ≤1, uses exact serial Gauss-Seidel path. When >1, uses parallel Jacobi iteration (JacobiShared + jacobiWorker + runJacobiSweep). Jacobi reads from previous sweep's values, guaranteeing determinism regardless of thread count.

2. Added defaultFixpointThreads() = getCpuCount() - 2 (minimum 1). macOS has no taskset/numactl — thread count is the only core-sharing lever.

3. Added --threads N flag to exp6_solve.zig main() and oracle_v2_build.zig main(), defaulting to defaultFixpointThreads().

4. Created src/t312_race_control.zig with 4 tests wired into zig build test:
   - Serial vs parallel agreement (tiny graph, 100 reps, 4 threads)
   - Serial vs parallel agreement (2 threads, 50 reps)
   - Serial vs parallel agreement (7 threads, 10 reps)
   - Seeded defect: missing join barrier causes stale reads (positive control)
   All pass in ReleaseFast.

5. Build: zig build, zig build deploy, tools/smoke.sh all pass. Full test suite: 384/384 tests pass.

=== PER-THREAD MEMORY ===
Shared: compact_list (~99M × 8 bytes = 792 MB read-only), map (~99M × ~16 bytes = ~1.6 GB read-only), L_tab + H_tab (~198 MB), L_next + H_next (~198 MB). Per-thread: only stack (~8 KB). Peak RSS with 4 threads expected: ~3.4 GB (within 4 GB cap).

=== AUDIT OF PRIOR ART (retro.zig B31) ===
The retro.zig parallel finisher (lines 1259-1750) uses a work-item-based pattern with per-thread output buffers and merge. The fixpoint pattern is simpler (disjoint writes, no merge needed). The Thread.spawn pattern (worker 0 on calling thread, spawn for rest, join all) and getCpuCount() usage were adopted; the per-thread-output approach was not needed for Jacobi.
